messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [Name]
Age: 31
Gender: Female
Admission date: [Date]
Discharge date: [Date]

HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient was admitted for radical resection of right renal carcinoma after CT scans revealed a solid cystic and low-density foci in the right kidney. The surgery was performed under general anesthesia. The kidney was opened, and a white mass of 4 cm size and fine papilla on the surface of the lump in the right kidney was observed. Postoperative pathology revealed Xp11.2 translocations/TFE3 gene fusions associated with renal cell carcinoma. The patient did not receive any other treatments and tolerated the surgery well.

IMPRESSION:
The patient underwent the successful resection of renal cell carcinoma associated with Xp11.2 translocations/TFE3 gene fusions. A follow-up examination one month after the operation showed no recurrence.

PLAN:
The patient will be monitored for any signs of recurrence of renal cell carcinoma. Further follow-up and imaging studies will be recommended as necessary.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
The patient should continue her hemodialysis without any changes. The patient should make sure to attend all scheduled follow-up appointments and imaging studies. Any unusual symptoms should be reported to their primary care physician immediately.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
None.

DISCHARGE DISPOSITION:
The patient was discharged in stable condition.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Radical resection of a right renal mass that proved to be Xp11.2 translocation/TFE3 fusion renal cell carcinoma makes this a malignant neoplasm of the kidney (excluding renal pelvis). Neoplasms belong to chapter C, and the kidney category is C64. The ongoing haemodialysis is a comorbidity and does not change the principal diagnosis.

CODE: C64
